findings.evidence: Criterion c2: version_status "published" requires the maintainer to publish a release identifier for this board and the version to copy it. The protocol excerpts (homepage, README, app.js) contain no release identifier for ResearchClawBench-40-tasks: README refers only to "ResearchClawBench", "40 tasks", and agent-level versions (e.g., EvoScientist v0.1.1), never a board version. The activity summary (SOURCE 4) confirms the board is still served but introduces no version. Row declares version_status "published" and version "40-tasks", implying a maintainer-published release identifier that does not exist.
findings.repair: Set version_status to "snapshot" and change version to the dated identity snapshot-<retrieval-date> (or otherwise align version with the snapshot vocabulary) because the protocol publishes no release identifier for this board. If a maintainer release identifier is later evidenced, update to "published" and copy that identifier.

uncertainties: The full leaderboard.json payload was not excerpted; the value-scale (lowest 12.412894736842105, highest 21.11692307692308) and 10 changed-row activity summary are owner-generated reads of the hash-verified capture, used for the range and status checks.

The version_guard's claims about leaderboard.json keys and the exact 40 task ids could not be independently verified against the raw JSON; they were checked only against README structure (10 domains x 4 tasks) and the guard text itself.
We are read-only and cannot re-execute the owner's hash, transport, or qualification checks; those are outside this review's scope.
